title: Claim that Jeroboam culted Apis is free invention—Scripture never says so; his craft aimed away from Jerusalem, not from Jehovah
source_text: XXXVIII. Sed quod ad primum attinet, gratis fingitur, & dicitur Jeroboam & posteros ejus, in vitulis, Apim Aegyptium, vel nescio quod aliud numen coluisse. Nam Scriptura nusquam id affirmat; imo contrarium potius innuit, ut thesibus superioribus ostensum est. Nec est cur putemus populum, qui nuper tanta Dei miracula viderat, tam subito ad Aegyptiacas superstitiones revolvendum fuisse, praesertim quum Rex ipse id minime intendisse videatur, cujus consilium erat populum a Jerusalem, non a Jehova, avertere.
pass_a_gloss: But as to the first, it is freely feigned, and said that Jeroboam and his posterity cultivated in the calves Apis the Egyptian, or I know not what other divinity. For Scripture nowhere affirms that; nay rather it hints the contrary, as was shown in the superior theses. Nor is there reason why we should think that a people who had recently seen so great miracles of God would so suddenly have been rolled back to Egyptian superstitions, especially when the King himself seems least to have intended that, whose counsel was to turn the people from Jerusalem, not from Jehovah.
pass_b_english: Jeroboam’s counsel was anti-Jerusalem, not anti-Jehovah—sudden Egypt-reversion is psychologically forced.
